ai.description: *Raorchestes lechiya* is a small frog (20–23 mm) with a yellowish-brown dorsum and dark brown lateral bands. It features a distinct white spot on the snout and granular skin with scattered tubercles.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Raorchestes lechiya* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, bright yellow or cream-colored patch on the groin and the hidden surfaces of its thighs.
ai.habitat: *Raorchestes lechiya* inhabits high-altitude montane evergreen forests (shola) and adjacent grasslands in the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations above 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: Raorchestes lechiya is a nocturnal frog that remains active during the night, often calling from foliage to attract mates within its high-altitude habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Raorchestes lechiya* exhibits direct development, bypassing the tadpole stage. It breeds during the monsoon, laying small clutches of eggs in arboreal nests.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Raorchestes lechiya* is endemic to the high-elevation shola forests of the Western Ghats in Kerala, India, typically found at altitudes above 1,800 meters.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Raorchestes lechiya* is a high-pitched, insect-like trill consisting of a series of rapid, pulsed notes heard within high-altitude shola forests.
